feedback: If a non-living or non-animal item is chosen, note that a minibeast is a living animal that moves, eats and grows.
If only insects are chosen, remind that worms, snails, spiders and woodlice are minibeasts too, even though they look different.
activities.intendedInsight: Checks whether the learner can recognise minibeasts and their hiding places and link them to the 'small, no backbone' idea.
learnerActions: Look at pictures and choose which creature is a minibeast.
Choose where you might find a given minibeast (e.g. a woodlouse) from picture options.
Say briefly why your choice is a minibeast (small, no backbone).
activities.title: Which is a minibeast, and where would you look?

feedback: If a learner says 'the snail is just a bug, not an animal', widen the category: show the snail moves, eats and grows like any animal — it's a small animal without a backbone.

If a learner says a beetle has tiny bones inside, introduce 'no backbone': many minibeasts have a hard covering on the outside instead of bones inside, but some (like worms) have neither — the shared feature is simply no backbone.

If a learner thinks a worm can't be an animal because it has no legs, explain that animals don't need legs: a worm is an animal because it moves — it wriggles — and eats, grows and is alive, even with no legs and no backbone.

For 'is a woodlouse more like a dog or a rock?': it's more like a dog, because both are living animals that move, eat and grow, while a rock is not alive and does not move, eat or grow by itself. (The dog has a backbone and the woodlouse does not, but both still count as animals.)
activities.intendedInsight: Minibeasts are animals too — they move, eat, grow and are alive; being an animal is not about being big or furry.
learnerActions: Join a friendly naturalist who asks 'shall we look under this log?' and reacts to what's found.

Say what you notice about each creature and answer the probe questions: 'A worm has no legs and no bones — how can it still be an animal?' and 'Is a woodlouse more like a dog or more like a rock? Why?'
Explain what a beetle and a dog both do that shows they are both animals.
activities.title: Talk it through with a bug-hunter guide
